design_note: Demonstrate duplicate event handling while rebuilding a budget projection from a snapshot. The duplicate delivery does not represent a second model invocation, and the cursor must commit atomically with the accounting update.

source.title: Event Sourcing pattern
source.concept: Snapshots allow replay from a recorded stream position, and duplicate event delivery requires idempotent projection updates to avoid counting the same change twice.
source.scope: Original model-turn ledger assumes atomic cursor and projection updates. It explains bookkeeping replay, not external exactly-once execution or a requirement to adopt event sourcing.

lesson.title: Replay an event once, even when delivered twice
lesson.intro: Snapshot E20 retains 8 unused model turns. Rebuilding the projection receives accounting events E21, E22, duplicate E22, and E23. Each unique event represents one already completed generation; replay invokes no model.

data.rule: Persist cursor and debit together. Replay restores settled usage; it reserves no new calls.

read: The snapshot already incorporates all accounting through E20.
A repeated event identity describes the same generation, not additional work.
Three unique events reduce 8 remaining turns to 5.
lesson.question: If E22 arrives a third time after E23, should the remaining allowance fall from 5 to 4?
lesson.answer: No. The projection has already incorporated E22 and its cursor has passed that position. Ignore the duplicate under the ordered-stream contract. The consumed allowance remains 3 turns since E20, leaving 5. Cursor advancement and the debit must be atomic so a crash cannot split them.
lesson.takeaway: An accounting projection counts accepted event identities, not delivery attempts.
lesson.assumption: Constructed ordered event stream and atomic projection/cursor commit. Turns were settled at generation; replay adds no reservation, model call or external effect.
